sentence: ICICI Bank delivered strong core operating performance with Net Interest Income expanding robustly and domestic loan growth reaching 15.6% year-on-year.
Asset quality continues to be pristine with Net NPA ratio at 0.43% and Provision Coverage Ratio exceeding 80%.
In Q2 FY25, ICICI Bank achieved healthy profit after tax growth of 14.5% year-on-year driven by sustained business banking momentum.
Return on Assets stood at an industry-leading 2.32% and Return on Equity exceeded 17.8%, underscoring our core operating profitability.
Our digital banking platforms processed record transaction volumes, driving fee income growth of 16.2% year-on-year.
Capital adequacy remains exceptionally strong with Tier-1 CAR above 16%, positioning the bank for sustained market share gains.
Granular deposit inflows accelerated across affluent and salaried customer segments, strengthening our funding stability.
Our technology investments in AI-powered credit underwriting continue to improve cost-to-income efficiency.
Q3 FY26 marked another quarter of superior execution for ICICI Bank, with Net Profit crossing Rs 12,400 Crore.
High-margin business banking and SME working capital lines grew 19.4% year-on-year, boosting overall profitability.
Systemic wholesale deposit rates stay volatile and CASA mobilization faces severe headwinds across the banking sector.
Near-term NIM trajectory is pressured by lagged deposit repricing, making margin expansion challenging in the immediate quarters.
Industry-wide microfinance and personal loan stress remains challenging, causing unsecured credit growth to slow down.
Retail savers shifting toward higher-yielding term deposits creates structural funding headwinds that compress CASA margins.
Immediate repo rate transmission on floating-rate loans creates near-term downward pressure and headwinds for Net Interest Margin.
Historical credit seasoning implies provision expenses could edge up from cyclical troughs under challenging macro conditions.
Export-oriented MSME working capital demand faces headwinds from global trade disruptions and tight liquidity.
Wholesale funding spreads remain volatile and elevated, creating downward pressure on treasury trading income.
Sustaining NIM above 4.30% remains challenging due to persistent deposit cost escalation across urban markets.
Rising household leverage in lower-ticket retail cohorts has increased delinquency risk across unsecured personal loans.
The Board of Directors met in Mumbai on Saturday to review the audited standalone and consolidated financial statements.
Total branch network stood at 6,613 branches and 17,120 ATMs across India at the end of the quarter.
Our domestic loan book comprises 53% retail advances, 21% business banking, and 26% corporate and institutional loans.
Around 49% of the domestic loan portfolio is linked to the RBI repo rate, while 19% is linked to MCLR.
Contingency provisioning buffer was maintained unchanged at Rs 13,100 Crore at the close of the fiscal year.
Future monetary policy adjustments remain subject to RBI MPC meetings scheduled over the next two quarters.
The diluted equity share base stood at 704.8 Crore shares of face value Rs 2 each as of the reporting date.
Average Liquidity Coverage Ratio for the quarter was reported at 121.5% under standard Basel III norms.
We will evaluate the updated RBI circular on project finance provisioning once final guidelines are notified.
Consolidated results include the financial statements of ICICI Prudential Life, ICICI Lombard, and ICICI AMC.

Q3 FY26 delivered record consolidated quarterly profit for Reliance Industries, propelled by festive consumer demand.
Cash flows from operations reached Rs 1.74 Lakh Crore, driving a powerful free cash flow inflection across the conglomerate.

O2C ethane and naphtha cracking margins remain depressed and challenging given sluggish global industrial recovery.
Global polymer overcapacity presents persistent margin headwinds and depresses downstream petrochemical profitability.
The transition period before New Energy gigafactories reach commercial utilization creates near-term return headwinds.

Hyper-competitive discounting by quick-commerce peers presents margin headwinds in urban grocery delivery.
O2C polyester and polymer deltas face ongoing downward pressure from regional supply additions in Asia.
Subscriber churn in lower-ARPU 2G cohorts rose temporarily following the telecom tariff adjustments.
Initial gigafactory ramp-up margins face downside risks from polysilicon price volatility and export tariff barriers.

Total physical retail store count stood at 18,836 stores covering 79.1 million square feet of retail area.
The Jamnagar refining complex processed 16.8 million metric tonnes of crude feedstock during the third quarter.

Total gross debt stood at Rs 3,45,000 Crore while cash and marketable securities were Rs 2,15,000 Crore at year-end.
Future telecom tariff adjustments remain subject to industry regulatory filings and market conditions.
Phase-1 of the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex is located across 5,000 acres in Jamnagar, Gujarat.
Average daily gas production from the KG-D6 basin was maintained at 28.5 MMSCMD during the quarter.
Depreciation and amortization charges reflect the capitalization of 5G spectrum assets under Ind AS accounting rules.
The Annual General Meeting of shareholders is scheduled to be held via video conferencing in August.
